guides.name: Spiritmaster PvP guide: outlast and control — Inven, Sujiro

$join: A Korean player's PvP guide built on outlasting the opponent rather than bursting them: keep debuffs and sustained damage rolling while high Status Effect Resist and Chance let you shrug off enemy control and land your own. Spirit's Benediction, Ancient Spirit, Kaisinel's Power and Siphon form the stigma core, with Command: Proxy and Seize Magic as swaps. Gear leans on Weapon Damage Boost and Accuracy, plus as much HP and Defense as you can fit.

tips.title: Two stat directions
tips.text: Either Weapon Damage Boost + Perfect + Accuracy (expensive, highest ceiling) or a Double-based setup (cheap and efficient). The author runs Weapon Damage Boost + Accuracy and uses soul imprints for lots of HP and Defense.

tips.title: Why HP and Defense
tips.text: Siphon's shield and healing potions scale with max HP. Spirit Protection is the class's only defensive passive, so stack Defense; with Command: Proxy active the author went past 75k Defense and survived 1-vs-many fights. Justice helps get Perfect and Defense together.

tips.title: PvP Damage Boost is a luxury
tips.text: PvP Damage Boost is strong but costly (limit break, Abyss manastones), and it falls off fast if your Attack can't beat the target's Defense.

tips.title: Gear path
tips.text: Weapon: a crafted or lava weapon is fine; PvP weapons add less damage than expected. Guard: a Legion guard first, it carries a lot of Damage Boost. Armor: start with the cheaper PvP set for its set bonus and PvP Damage Tolerance, then move to Legion armor (it needs many medals). Accessories matter least; the cheaper set gives Damage Boost.

tips.title: Soul imprint options
tips.text: Weapon/guard: Combat Speed, Weapon Damage Boost, Might, Precision, Status Effect Chance, Multi-Hit, Accuracy, Attack. Armor: Damage Boost or Tolerance, Constitution, Double Resist, Status Effect Resist, Willpower and passive skill lines (Spirit Strike first). Necklace/earrings: Accuracy, Intelligence, passives; rings: active skills. Slots are few, so lock in the must-haves first.

tips.title: Stigma picks
tips.text: Spirit's Benediction and Ancient Spirit are fixed. Kaisinel's Power covers Status Effect Resist/Chance and Accuracy (its Block/Evasion option is weak) and is needed for Magic Block. Siphon heals and shields. Command: Proxy is the anti-burst swap; Seize Magic strips buffs; Corrode and Cursed Cloud add DoTs but get cleansed.

tips.title: Stigmas the author skips
tips.text: Jointstrike: Destructive Attack is risky burst unless you have Evasion/Block/weapon options for it; Assault Terror is only for chasing; Flame Blessing is not worth it; Cry of Terror loses to the active Soul's Cry.

tips.title: Skill levels
tips.text: Combustion and Elemental Fusion at 20; Cold Shock, Jointstrike: Curse, Dimensional Control and the spirit skills at 16 or higher, never below 12. Get passives through Arcana and soul imprints.

$join: Written summary of a Korean video on how top Spiritmasters set up skills, with a separate PvP specialization list. Combustion and Elemental Fusion go to 20, Soul's Cry and Jointstrike: Curse get cooldown and control options, and Dimensional Control joins at 16 for its Root. The stigma core is Spirit's Benediction, Ancient Spirit and Corrode, and a short burst combo is shown deleting a high-power Chanter.

tips.title: PvP specializations
tips.text: Combustion 3/4/5, Water Spirit 2/3/5, Jointstrike: Curse 3/4, Soul's Cry 1/4/5. Elemental Fusion: 1+3 or 2+3 while you have two slots, 1/3/5 at level 20.

tips.title: Dimensional Control
tips.text: Mainly a PvP tool: at level 16 it gets the Root option and becomes worth a slot. Below 16 the video doesn't recommend it, and it isn't used in PvE.

tips.title: Stigma priority
tips.text: Spirit's Benediction to 20 first, then Ancient Spirit to 15; Corrode is fine at level 1. The fourth slot is open (Siphon or Magic Block); the final set uses Jointstrike: Destructive Attack.

tips.title: Burst combo
tips.text: Spirit's Benediction, Ancient Spirit, Corrode, Soul's Cry twice, then Elemental Fusion. Line them up on keys you can hit in one quick sequence.

tips.title: Passives
tips.text: Heroic-grade passives first: Spirit Strike, Mental Focus, Spirit Protection and Corrode. Revitalization Contract and Spirit Revitalization come later.

tips.title: No single right answer
tips.text: The author stresses that specializations should fit your own play style; the lists are a starting point, not a rule.

$join: The PvP section of a global-version build guide. It argues that Spiritmaster PvP is less about a perfect Elemental Fusion loop and more about disrupting the enemy so your summons can keep up the pressure safely. Stats go to PvP Accuracy and Status Effect Chance first, then survival; Ancient Spirit and Spirit's Benediction stay, with Command: Proxy and Seize Magic added for PvP.

tips.title: Control and survival over damage
tips.text: PvP Accuracy and Status Effect Chance first so your control lands, then HP and PvP Damage Tolerance, then Status Effect Resist, and only then PvP damage and other offense.

tips.title: PvP stigmas
tips.text: Keep Ancient Spirit and Spirit's Benediction for the summon engine, add Command: Proxy for when you are focused and Seize Magic against enemy buffs. Against healers, Corrode can take Proxy's slot.

tips.title: Keep PvP buttons manual
tips.text: Fear, Command: Proxy, Seize Magic and Defiance should not sit in an automatic sequence: their value depends on what the enemy has already used.

tips.title: Matchups
tips.text: Against melee, always keep a defensive answer for their gap closer. Against ranged, reposition rather than take one more exposed cast. In the Abyss, coordinate Fear and dispels with your group.

tips.title: Daevanion and gear (general part)
tips.text: Outside the PvP section the article takes core skill-level nodes first, then Combat Speed, Cooldown Reduction, Damage Boost, Critical Damage Boost and Multi-Hit, and notes that rings can add levels to Elemental Fusion, Combustion and Fire Spirit.
